incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993, Public Act 1993 No 105, New Zealand; sections 12-14 (Incorporation, Registration and Effect of Registration), sections 22-24 (Company Name Rules), section 151 (Board of Directors Requirements), and section 184 (Registered Office); together with the New Zealand Business Number Act 2016 for automatic NZBN issuance on incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company filed electronically through the New Zealand Companies Office online portal pursuant to section 12 of the Companies Act 1993.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up share capital, no authorised capital concept, and no escrow, blocked-account, or pre-deposit capital rule. Shares may be issued fully paid, partly paid, or for non-cash consideration subject to the directors' determination that the consideration is fair and adequate. The company must have at least one share, one shareholder, and one director, but no minimum monetary subscription is required before incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED

THIS RESOLUTION is made on the date first written below by the directors of [COMPANY NAME] Limited (the Company), a company incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 of New Zealand, pursuant to that Act and the constitution of the Company.

1. INCORPORATION AND REGISTERED OFFICE
RESOLVED: THAT the incorporation of the Company under the Companies Act 1993, the issue of the New Zealand Business Number, and all preliminary statutory filings made by the formation agent be and they are hereby acknowledged, ratified, and approved in all respects. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT the registered office of the Company be and it is hereby fixed at [Street Address, City, New Zealand], and that the directors be and they are hereby authorised to deliver and file the registered office address with the Registrar of Companies under section 184 of the Companies Act 1993, and to change that address from time to time as the Board may determine.

2. SHARE CAPITAL, SUBSCRIPTION, AND ALLOTMENT
RESOLVED: THAT the proposed allotment of shares to the subscribers named in the shareholder register and subscription schedule presented to this Board be and it is hereby approved and confirmed. The Board determines that the consideration payable for each share is as set out in each subscriber's share application, and that such consideration is fair and reasonable to the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT the directors are authorised to issue, allot, record, and register the shares, to accept cash or non-cash consideration, to classify shares into any classes permitted by the constitution, and to make all appropriate entries in the share register. The Board confirms that New Zealand law imposes no minimum paid-up share capital and no escrow or blocked funds requirement.

3. BANKING ARRANGEMENTS
RESOLVED: THAT the Company's banking relationship be and it is hereby established with a licensed New Zealand trading bank selected by the directors. The directors be and they are hereby authorised to open corporate bank accounts in the name of the Company, to complete and execute all banking mandates, resolutions, account opening documents, and electronic banking agreements, and to appoint any two directors or such other officers as the Board may designate as authorised signatories. The bank is authorised to rely upon this resolution until written notice of revocation is received by the bank.

4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS
RESOLVED: THAT [Full Name] and [Full Name] be and they are hereby appointed as directors of the Company, effective immediately, and that at least one appointed director remains resident in New Zealand as required by section 151 of the Companies Act 1993. RESOLVED FURTHER: THAT [Full Name] be appointed Chairperson, and [Full Name] be appointed Chief Executive Officer and Company Secretary, such office being permissive and not mandatory, with authority to execute contracts and manage the day-to-day affairs of the Company pending further Board direction.

5. GENERAL AUTHORITY
RESOLVED: THAT all actions taken by any director, officer, and agent of the Company consistent with the purposes of these resolutions be and they are hereby ratified, confirmed, and approved in all respects. The directors be and they are hereby authorised to take any ancillary steps, execute any documents, and give any notices necessary to give full force and effect to this resolution.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the directors have executed this resolution as an act of the Company on [Date].

______________________
Director: [Full Name]

______________________
Director: [Full Name]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Clearance, Entity Design, and Statutory Data Assembly
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, Registrar of Companies, MBIE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a statutory name search on the New Zealand Companies Register to confirm the proposed company name is available, is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, and does not contravene the name restrictions in sections 22-24 of the Companies Act 1993. Because the entity is to be a limited liability company, the name must include the word Limited or Ltd. If the client wishes to reserve the name before incorporation, file an online name reservation through the Companies Office portal, which holds the name for 20 working days. Meanwhile, assemble all required statutory particulars: full legal names, dates and places of birth, residential addresses, and consent of each proposed director; proposed shareholders and share allocation; a New Zealand street address for the registered office; the principal place of business; and the proposed constitution if a bespoke constitution is desired. Confirm that at least one director is resident in New Zealand or that a compliant local agent is appointed if all directors are non-resident.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name ending in Limited or Ltd
Full legal names, birth details, and residential addresses of all proposed directors
Written consents to act as director from each proposed director
Shareholder full legal names, shareholdings, and share class designations
New Zealand registered office street address and owner consent
Principal place of business address in New Zealand
Constitution if adopting bespoke constitutional provisions
Power of attorney or authorisation to the formation agent if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office flags the name or any director data, the portal will issue a request for further information. The formation agent must cure the query by amending the deficient fields or filing a fresh name reservation within 20 working days. If the name is indistinguishable or otherwise prohibited, submit an alternative name and continue with the same incorporation dossier.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitutional Instruments and Statutory Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board-designated formation counsel or a licensed New Zealand corporate lawyer
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the constitution only if the client does not want to rely on the default rules of the Companies Act 1993. The constitution must address share class rights, voting rights, director appointment powers, director quorum, conflict of interest procedures, share transfer restrictions, and indemnity provisions. Prepare or acquire all statutory consents: each director must sign a consent to act as director, each subscriber must sign a share application or subscription letter, and the owner of the proposed registered office address must consent to its use. If any shares are to be issued for non-cash consideration, receive a valuation report or board record showing that the consideration is fair and adequate. Verify that the registered office is a physical New Zealand street address, not a postal box. The administrative minutes of this pre-incorporation activity must be retained for the company records and later presented to the first Board.
required_dossiers: Signed constitution, if adopted, endorsed by each initially named director
Signed consent to act as director for each director
Signed share application and subscription letters for each initial shareholder
Draft share register entries showing names, addresses, share classes, and consideration paid
Written consent from owner of the registered office premises
Valuation report or board determination for non-cash consideration, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any consent document is incomplete, incorrect, or challenged by the Registrar, execute a corrected consent or subscription letter, re-verify the signatory's identity, and upload the revised document into the Companies Office portal before final lodgment. No loss of priority will occur if the correction is made within the permitted response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Lodgment of Incorporation Application and Payment of Official Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies via the New Zealand Companies Office online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the New Zealand Companies Office online portal using the authorised agent's credentials. Select register a company and complete Form 1 - Application for Registration of a Company. Enter the proposed name, the full statutory details of each director and shareholder, the exact share allocation, the registered office address, the principal place of business address, and the designated email and postal addresses. Attach the constitution, director consents, and any share valuation documents. Review the system-generated application summary for accuracy. Pay the applicable electronic filing fee, currently approximately NZ$105.00 or USD 64, using an accepted payment method. Submit the application electronically. Upon successful verification, the Registrar will register the company under section 13 of the Companies Act 1993, issue a Certificate of Incorporation, and automatically allocate a New Zealand Business Number. The Certificate of Incorporation is conclusive evidence of formation and must be stored in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Completed online Form 1 fields for all directors and shareholders
Proposed constitution in PDF format if adopted
Executed director consent forms uploaded as attachments
Share allotment schedule and consideration details
Registered office address and principal place of business details
Proof of payment of the electronic incorporation filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, the Companies Office will issue a Request for Further Information through the online portal. The applicant has a finite response period, typically 10 working days, to address the query and resubmit the corrected information. If the application is rejected outright, refile a fresh Form 1 with corrected data and, if necessary, request internal review of the Registrar's decision under the administrative review provisions of the Companies Act 1993.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax, Banking, and Statutory Officer Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department of New Zealand, a licensed New Zealand trading bank, and the company's first Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after receiving the Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN, register the Company with the Inland Revenue Department for income tax through the NZBN online portal. Register for GST if annual taxable supplies are expected to exceed NZD 60,000, or elect voluntary GST registration where appropriate. Register as an employer if staff will be hired. Convene the First Board resolution described in this dossier to formally allot shares, adopt the registered office, open a bank account, and appoint directors and officers. Bring the Certificate of Incorporation, NZBN certificate, constitution, executed first Board resolution, director identification, and proof of address to a licensed New Zealand bank. Complete the bank's AML/CFT onboarding, enhanced due diligence questionnaires, and expected electronic payment rail declarations for Stripe and PayPal. Provide source-of-funds and beneficial ownership declarations because online sales of jewelry, watches, and fashion items are classified as medium-risk under New Zealand's Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar of Companies
New Zealand Business Number certificate
Executed pro-forma First Board Resolution
Constitution, if any, certified by a director
Company extract from the Companies Register dated within 30 days
Director passports, national IDs, and proof of residential address
Shareholder register and ultimate beneficial owner schedule
Source of funds and source of wealth declarations
AML/CFT corporate onboarding forms for the bank
GST and income tax registration confirmations from Inland Revenue
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines or delays onboarding due to AML/CFT concerns, provide expanded source-of-wealth evidence, corporate structure charts, and confirmation of the physical registered office. If Inland Revenue queries the GST registration, correct the projected turnover figures and resubmit through the NZBN portal. If any officer appointment is rejected by the bank, pass a supplemental board resolution and file updated officer details with the Companies Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registers, Annual Return Calendar, and Operational Licensing Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company Board of Directors and New Zealand Companies Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Establish and maintain the company's statutory registers, including the share register, director register, director interest register, and charges register, at the registered office or through an approved registry provider. Record the first Board meeting minutes and all subsequent Board resolutions. Place the annual return filing date on the company compliance calendar; the Companies Office will prompt the company each year. Verify that the company's planned online retail operations under ISIC 4791 do not constitute a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity and therefore do not require an industrial operating license, Environmental Impact Assessment, or Civil Defense fire permit. If a physical inventory warehouse is added later, stop and secure the applicable local council building certificate, Fire and Emergency New Zealand fire safety clearance, and WorkSafe New Zealand notification under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015. File any future change of registered office or director details with the Registrar within the statutory notice periods. Retain all statutory records for at least seven years.
required_dossiers: Statutory registers, including share register and director register
First Board minutes and executed resolutions
Annual return filing calendar and Companies Office log-in credentials
Certified copy of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Local authority building and fire compliance evidence, only if a physical warehouse is later occupied
Health and safety policy documentation, only if employees are engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return filing is missed or the company is administratively removed or dissolved, apply for restoration under the Companies Act 1993 within two years, pay all outstanding fees, and file the overdue annual return immediately. If the Companies Office queries registrable changes, file the corresponding amendment notice through the online portal and pay the small amendment fee. Any future industrial licensing obligation triggered by adding a physical warehouse must be cured by applying to the appropriate local council and Fire and Emergency New Zealand before operations commence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the entity is structured as ISIC 4791 online merchandising of fashion jewelry and fine timepieces and does not own or operate a physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing facility.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating licence is mandated for pure online retail. The company remains subject to the Fair Trading Act 1986 and the Consumer Guarantees Act 1993 as ordinary consumer protection law, but these are not industrial licenses.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority and regional councils under the Resource Management Act 1991 have no jurisdiction for an online retail-only activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - ISIC 4791 online retail falls outside the scheduled activities requiring a full Environmental Impact Assessment, environmental registration, or discharge permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the operation has no point-source wastewater discharges, no volatile organic compound emissions, no combustion activities, and no hazardous waste storage or handling. If the company later opens a physical warehouse, it must separately assess National Environmental Standards for hazardous substances and any local district plan requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defense fire permit, structural load inspection, or industrial workplace safety approval is triggered by an online-only retail model. If the company later occupies an office or warehouse, it must comply with Fire and Emergency New Zealand fire safety requirements, the Building Act 2004 occupancy certification, and the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, ordinary office worker duties being covered by general, non-industrial workplace safety obligations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand, also known as Te Tari Taake. The primary online taxpayer portal is myIR. Export customs control is administered separately by the New Zealand Customs Service through its Trade Single Window.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain legal standing in New Zealand. A foreign non-resident entity must either incorporate a New Zealand Limited Company or register as an overseas company with the New Zealand Companies Office. This generates a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN). Step 2: Apply to Inland Revenue for a company IRD number using the myIR for Business online service. The IRD number is the taxpayer identification number used for all New Zealand tax obligations including income tax and GST. Step 3: Where a taxable activity is carried on in New Zealand and annual taxable supplies are NZD 60,000 or more, apply for GST registration through myIR. The GST registration is recorded under the same IRD number. Step 4: If the entity will have New Zealand employees, register for PAYE; if paying assessable income from New Zealand to non-residents, register for Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) obligations. Step 5: Appoint and retain a New Zealand address for service if required by the Companies Act regime for overseas companies, so that Inland Revenue and Customs notices can be validly served. Supporting documents include the certificate of incorporation or overseas company registration, NZBN certificate, registered office details, director and beneficial ownership information, and a home-jurisdiction tax residence certificate if treaty relief is sought.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. New Zealand does not have a US-style check-the-box election for ordinary limited companies. A New Zealand Limited Company is automatically subject to entity-level taxation. Hybrid mismatch rules apply under the Income Tax Act 2007 and the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018. Look-through company status is a separate statutory eligibility category for closely held companies, not a general election for an ordinary NZ Ltd.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period. Non-resident suppliers of remote services and low-value goods supplied to New Zealand consumers are also required to register for GST once those supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance regime, no anti-fraud digital stamping requirement, and no IRD API pre-clearance for invoices. Tax invoices must nevertheless meet the content requirements of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985. Electronic invoicing is voluntary and operates on the New Zealand e-Invoicing network using the Peppol framework through certified access points. GST returns are filed through Inland Revenue's myIR portal, and records supporting tax invoices and zero-rated exports must be retained under the Tax Administration Act 1994.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, sections 11 and 11A, goods may be zero-rated when supplied for export and physically removed from New Zealand. For an online jewellery and watches business, the standard qualifying supply is a sale of physical goods to an overseas customer where the supplier exports the goods from New Zealand in the course of the supply and retains evidence of export. Qualifying offshore services supplied to non-resident recipients may also be zero-rated if not performed in New Zealand or not connected with New Zealand land. The exporter is entitled to claim input tax credits on costs attributable to the zero-rated export supply, and resulting GST refunds are payable by Inland Revenue.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service electronic Export Entry declaration lodged through the Trade Single Window
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing the goods were consigned to the overseas customer
Commercial invoice and packing list identifying the exported jewellery, watches and fashion items
Proof of physical departure such as customs export clearance, carrier cargo manifest, or freight forwarder certification
Bank records evidencing receipt of foreign currency payment from the offshore buyer, including SWIFT MT103 or equivalent remittance credit advice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If Inland Revenue determines that export zero-rating is not substantiated, the supply is re-classified as taxable at 15% GST and the supplier is re-assessed for the output tax on the full consideration, with late payment interest. Shortfall penalties apply under sections 141A to 141E of the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for lack of reasonable care or an unacceptable tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion. Criminal prosecution may also follow for fraudulent export zero-rating claims, and the exporter may be liable for a retrospective clawback of all refunds previously paid.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand - no separate Foreign Exchange Administration exists; exchange controls were abolished in 1984 and no central bank approval is required for outward or inward FX transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully floating exchange-rate regime with no exchange controls. The New Zealand dollar is freely convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no central-bank approvals, no foreign-exchange budget, and no surrender requirements for export receipts. Non-resident equity investment, shareholder loans, trade payments, and profit remittances can be paid in and out without foreign-exchange authorisation. For an e-commerce jewellery and fine-watch trading company, the main practical hurdles are not currency-convertibility limits but tax clearances: dividends and interest paid to non-residents are subject to non-resident withholding tax, often reduced by double-tax agreements and the Approved Issuer Levy on New Zealand source interest. Banks also classify unusually large or structurally illogical payments for AML/CFT review. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand maintains the currency and prudential stability of the banking system, but it does not approve individual FX transactions. Thus, the treasury can structure inward equity injections, offshore settlement accounts, and external trade disbursements with full market-based conversion and no earmarked surrender requirement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency receipts in domestic or offshore bank accounts indefinitely and may convert to New Zealand dollars at commercial market rates without approval. Banks may require the underlying export invoice, packing list, customs export declaration, or transport waybill to classify the inwards remittance correctly for statistical reporting and to avoid a suspicious transaction report.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Conditional Medium for settlement liquidity, but Low as the primary treasury relationship. New Zealand does not maintain a domestic electronic-money-institution (EMI) licensing category equivalent to the EU/UK EMI regime. Payment service providers, including offshore digital EMIs, may lawfully operate if they are registered on the Financial Service Providers Register or rely on an applicable overseas licensing arrangement, and if they comply with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. Offshore EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex, or specialist FX payment platforms are not legally barred from servicing New Zealand corporate entities, provided their New Zealand offering is compliant; however, they do not hold a full banking licence and are not covered by the existing bank deposit compensation arrangements. For an e-commerce jewellery/watches treasury, EMIs are acceptable for merchant settlement and low-value disbursements, especially when integrated with Stripe or PayPal, but they should not replace a domestic tier-1 bank for capital injection, LC issuance, high-value trade payments, or capital verification evidence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory requirement forces all directors to appear physically in a New Zealand bank branch. Banks generally permit remote onboarding using certified passports, electronic identity verification, and a live video interview with the statutory directors or authorised signatories. Consular proxy or notary-verified signatures may be accepted for signature witnessing, but they do not replace the bank's independent obligation to identify the ultimate beneficial owners. Under the Medium-Risk Enhanced classification of jewellery/watch e-commerce, the bank's compliance committee may require an additional video interview with the company secretary, a director, or the beneficial owner, and may request a local New Zealand registered office address. Practical mandate: at least one director or authorised signatory must complete a video KYC interview, all directors must submit certified photo ID and proof of residential address, and the accounting/company-formation agent must provide a current Certificate of Incorporation and director/UBO register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership is opaque because the New Zealand Ltd is held through a discretionary trust, nominee arrangement, or an offshore structure with no clear 25% natural-person owner visible on the public register.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified trust deed and all deed amendments; trustee and protector resolutions; a register of identifiable discretionary beneficiaries and their vested interests; source-of-wealth statements for the settlor and trustee; a 25% economic interest analysis; any foreign trust disclosure filing; and certified passports or national ID cards of the trustee, protector, settlor, and any controlling beneficiary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering typologies in the high-value jewellery/fine-watch sector, including invoice inflation, counterfeit goods, false customs valuations, and inconsistent settlement values across e-commerce markets.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal supplier agreements and approved vendor list; original supplier invoices and purchase orders; incoterm declarations on shipping documents; customs entry and export declarations; independent pre-shipment inspection certificates; authenticity certificates for branded watches and jewellery; insurance valuation reports; SKU-level inventory reconciliation; and a documented invoice-to-payment matching control signed by the finance director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from a non-resident shareholder or related party where the source of funds is not self-evident, or where funds are received from high-risk jurisdictions or jointly controlled third-party accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed board resolution authorising the share allotment or shareholder loan; updated share register and shareholder loan agreement; bank reference letters for the remitting bank; a source-of-wealth report for funding amounts above the bank's high-value threshold; six months of upstream bank statements showing the accumulation of funds; tax residency certificates for the shareholder; and an accountant-issued capital verification certificate prepared by a New Zealand chartered accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list, PEP-listing, or adverse-media hit on a director, beneficial owner, counterparty, or payment corridor, particularly where the counterparty is based in a jurisdiction with weak AML enforcement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete sanctions and PEP screening reports with the exact hit detail; adverse-media narrative and independent news scan; an independent legal opinion on political exposure and the commercial rationale; a statement of source of wealth for the named person; board resolutions confirming the legitimate purpose of the relationship; and if the hit cannot be resolved, a commitment to restructure the ownership or payment corridor prior to account opening.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funds must be remitted through the regulated banking system using SWIFT MT103 from the overseas remitting bank. New Zealand does not use IBAN; the sending bank must use the receiving bank's SWIFT BIC plus the company's New Zealand bank account number in the beneficiary field. The remittance advice should state the exact purpose, such as share capital contribution or shareholder loan, and reference the board resolution, subscription agreement, or loan agreement. The receiving bank will apply standard source-of-funds due diligence, so send the supporting board resolution, shareholder register, source-of-wealth report, and signed loan agreement in advance to prevent quarantine. After the funds are cleared, a New Zealand chartered accountant should issue a formal capital verification certificate based on the bank credit statement, the share register, and the board minutes. For any foreign direct investment above the statutory screening threshold, apply for the relevant Overseas Investment Act consent before making the transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For first-time, high-value jewellery or fine-watch supplier payments, use an irrevocable confirmed commercial Letter of Credit issued by the New Zealand clearing bank in favour of the overseas supplier, with a sight draft and the required inspection certificate. For established counterparties and repeat funding of inventory, use SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers with the invoice number, purchase order number, incoterm, and customs tariff line in the payment reference. Documentary collections are also permissible for post-shipment settlement where the supplier retains title risk. All disbursements should be executed only from the tier-1 corporate account, not from merchant platform balances, and should be reconciled against Stripe, PayPal, and other settlement statements. Cash, crypto-currency, and unrestricted third-party payment methods are not acceptable for treasury-scale trade disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable NZD/USD forward contracts up to 12 months matched to underlying trade receivables or inventory purchases
FX swaps for rolling treasury liquidity between NZD and USD/EUR/CNH settlement balances without taking speculative open positions
Cross-currency swaps or non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts only when a booked commercial loan, trade invoice, or confirmed purchase order creates the underlying exposure
NDF hedges for invoices denominated in currencies with offshore convertibility constraints, executed strictly through the authorised tier-1 dealing desk or a licensed derivatives counterparty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Every calendar year within 10 working days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation; filing is accepted starting 1 month before the anniversary, and the 10-working-day grace period ends at midnight on the final working day
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a NZD 200 late penalty; continued non-filing triggers a section 318 removal notice from the Registrar; if no valid annual return or cause is shown within 20 working days of the notice, the Registrar publishes intention to remove the company from the New Zealand Register and the company is dissolved and struck off, with possible director disqualification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of Appointment or Resignation of Director, Director Consent, and Change of Registered Office or Address for Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 working days of the trigger event; maintained continuously and reconciled on each annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to notify is an offence under the Companies Act 1993 carrying fines up to NZD 50,000 and continuing penalties for persistent default; the company cannot rely on undocumented director or registered-office changes against third parties, and the Registrar may escalate non-compliance to removal and strike-off proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Directors Statement and, if statutorily required, Independent Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board and shareholders; New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE) for filing where the company is a non-SME large company, FMC reporting entity or issuer; Financial Markets Authority (FMA) for auditor oversight where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be prepared and signed by directors within 5 months after balance date; audited statements and the auditor's report must be made available to shareholders in the annual report not less than 10 working days before the annual meeting; if a filing obligation applies, file with the Companies Office within 10 working days after the annual report is sent to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; a director may be liable for fines up to NZD 100,000, plus an additional NZD 10,000 for each day the offence continues, and the matter may be referred to the Registrar, Financial Markets Authority, or Courts with possible director disqualification

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Share Register Update and Annual Confirmation of Shareholdings and Ownership within Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory records; consolidated ownership entry on the New Zealand Companies Register through the Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Each share transfer instrument must be registered in the Register of Members within 10 working days of the board receiving or executing the transfer; the annual return must confirm all shareholdings as at the annual return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain the register is an offence carrying fines up to NZD 50,000; an incorrect annual return may be treated as a false statutory declaration subjecting the company and directors to fines up to NZD 100,000 and possible imprisonment, and the Court may order register rectification and damages

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Companies Act 1993 and Financial Reporting Act 2013, a statutory independent audit by a certified auditor is mandatory when any of the following applies: (1) the company has public accountability or is an FMC reporting entity, issuer, licensed insurer, or licensed non-bank deposit taker; (2) for two consecutive annual reporting periods the company exceeds at least two of the quantitative gateways of total consolidated assets exceeding NZD 5.5 million, annual consolidated operating revenue exceeding NZD 11.1 million, or average full-time-equivalent employees exceeding 25; (3) the company exceeds NZD 30 million annual revenue or NZD 60 million total assets, triggering Tier 1 full NZ IFRS and audit; (4) shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting rights validly demand an audit or the constitution mandates one; (5) the company belongs to a group required to prepare consolidated audited financial statements and no group exemption applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Applicable accounting standards under the New Zealand Accounting Standards Framework and the Financial Reporting Act 2013: Tier 1 full New Zealand equivalents to IFRS (NZ IFRS) for large or publicly accountable entities; Tier 2 NZ IFRS Reduced Disclosure Regime for non-publicly accountable entities below the Tier 1 size gateways; and the simplified financial reporting framework for small-to-medium enterprises (SMEs). All statutory financial statements are expressed in New Zealand dollars and in English.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not maintain a separate annual beneficial-ownership return for a standard non-issuer NZ Ltd. Ownership is evidenced by the statutory Register of Members and by the shareholding confirmation in the annual return to the Registrar of Companies. A share transfer, issue, or redemption must be recorded in the Register of Members within 10 working days after the board registers the instrument. There is no 30-day UBO filing window for an ordinary Ltd; however, if the company is an AML/CFT reporting entity it must keep beneficial-owner records and refresh customer due diligence at least every 24 months, and within 30 days of becoming aware of a material change in beneficial ownership where the risk assessment requires it. The annual return simply confirms the then-current share register as at the annual-return date.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 25,000 per annum where mandatory; USD 0 for a statutory audit-exempt SME

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand levies a flat 28% company tax rate and has no general tax holiday or patent box regime. An R&D tax incentive provides a 15% refundable tax credit on eligible research and development expenditure, which may reduce the effective rate for technology-led e-commerce operations. No state or provincial corporate income tax applies; imputation credits attach to shareholder dividends and may lower the combined tax burden for NZ-resident shareholders.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 Company Income Tax Return filed through Inland Revenue myIR online portal; NZ company tax file number (IRD number) must be active.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; provisional tax is payable in three instalments for residual income tax over NZD 5,000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 is due by 7 July for electronic filing (7 June for paper). Non-standard balance dates require filing on or before the last day of the fourth month following the balance date, unless a tax agent extension applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, IRD number, registered office, principal place of business, directors and shareholder details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare whether the entity is tax resident in New Zealand under ITA 2007 s YD 2. If central management and control are outside New Zealand, dual-residence tie-breaker rules in the applicable DTA must be assessed. Record all non-resident shareholdings and ultimate beneficial owners, including trust and nominee structures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Balance Date and Accounting Period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year-end and income year covered by the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Align the NZ tax year with the 31 March standard, or use an approved non-standard balance date. For online jewellery and watch sales, allocate Stripe and PayPal settlement amounts to the correct income year using bank-value-date and refund cut-off adjustments; foreign exchange gains and losses must be separately reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from online merchandising of fashion jewellery, watches, accessories and related e-commerce revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise all income derived from New Zealand. Cross-border digital sales must be analysed under the business profits article of the DTA; if no New Zealand permanent establishment exists, the non-resident may not be taxable in New Zealand, but the NZ company must still report its own assessable income and verify that any foreign bookkeeper or staff activity in NZ does not create a PE for the foreign owner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, platform and payment gateway fees, logistics, packaging, marketing, salaries, rent, depreciation and administrative overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions only where expenses are incurred in deriving assessable income and are not capital, private or non-deductible. Management fees and royalties paid to overseas associates must satisfy the arm's-length standard and must have NRWT withheld at 15% unless treaty relief is substantiated; otherwise the deduction may be denied under the associated-party rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Interest, Dividends, Royalties and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: New Zealand-sourced passive income, foreign dividend income, RWT credits, NRWT credits and imputation credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose non-resident withholding tax paid on outbound interest, dividend and royalty flows. If the company receives foreign dividends, test the foreign dividend exemption or absorption rules. For non-resident shareholders claiming treaty benefits, the relevant tax residency certificate and beneficial ownership declaration must be attached to the payer before a reduced dividend rate may be applied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Related-Party Transactions and Transfer Pricing Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border purchases of jewellery, intercompany service fees, IP licence payments, loan interest, and sales commission paid to associated enterprises.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare and file the related-party disclosure schedule. Every intercompany transaction must be priced at arm's length using the most appropriate OECD method: CUP, resale price, cost plus, TNMM or profit split. New Zealand Inland Revenue may reconstruct the arrangement under ITA 2007 subpart GC where the economic substance of the e-commerce business, inventory risk and strategic decisions are located in New Zealand but profits are shifted offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Net Taxable Income and Loss Utilisation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciled net profit after expenses, transfer pricing adjustments, non-deductible items, and any brought-forward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify shareholder continuity for loss utilisation. Where non-resident ownership has changed by more than the permitted continuity percentage, the company loses its loss carry-forwards. In this whitepaper model the carry-forward limitation is set at 5 years; reconcile the tax loss schedule and imputation credit account before entering the loss amount.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Tax Payable, Refund and NRWT Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of residual income tax, provisional tax credits, imputation credits and net company tax payable or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Certify that final dividends paid or credited to non-residents have been subjected to NRWT at the statutory 30% rate unless a reduced DTA rate was properly claimed. If over-withholding occurred, the non-resident shareholder claims the refund; the company cannot unilaterally refund NRWT without Inland Revenue authority. Both the IR4 and the imputation return must agree with the NRWT schedule.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the IR4 attracts a NZD 250 late filing penalty, with additional NZD 250 penalties after 30 days and after 90 days if the return remains outstanding. Late payment penalties begin at 1% of the unpaid tax on the day after the due date, an additional 4% on day seven, and a further 1% for each month or part-month thereafter. Deliberate non-filing or false filing exposes the company to shortfall penalties of 20% to 150% under Tax Administration Act 1994 ss 141A-141E and criminal prosecution for tax evasion, carrying fines of up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years for individuals involved.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends paid or credited by a New Zealand company to a non-resident shareholder, before any DTA reduction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident recipient must: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the jurisdiction in which it is resident; (2) provide the certificate, together with a completed non-resident withholding tax reduced-rate declaration and a beneficial ownership statement, to the New Zealand company prior to payment; (3) demonstrate that the recipient has the economic substance to be regarded as the beneficial owner and is not a conduit or back-to-back nominee; and (4) provide any additional information required by the applicable DTA, such as substantial-holding thresholds for a 5% dividend rate and minimum holding periods. The New Zealand company must retain these documents in its tax files and file the relevant NRWT reconciliation with Inland Revenue; over-withheld NRWT may be refunded only through a claim by the non-resident in accordance with Tax Administration Act 1994 rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT is 15% on interest and 15% on royalties. Under New Zealand's bilateral DTAs, interest rates are commonly reduced to 10% or 15%, and royalties are commonly reduced to 5% or 10%, depending on the treaty partner and the beneficial ownership of the income. The Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may apply to certain interest payments but does not apply to royalties or dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NZD 1,000,000 aggregate cross-border related-party transactions is the administrative threshold commonly triggering mandatory contemporaneous Local File preparation in New Zealand; multinational groups with consolidated group revenue above NZD 1,125,000,000 are expected to prepare a Master File and Country-by-Country Report.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not apply Gulf-Cooperation-Council-style Economic Substance Regulations, but economic substance is enforced through tax residence, permanent establishment, general anti-avoidance and transfer pricing rules. Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) for an online jewellery and watch business are the functions of product sourcing, inventory risk-taking, pricing strategy, customer contracting, payment acceptance, marketing and after-sales service. If these activities are actually performed in New Zealand while profits are booked offshore, Inland Revenue will reallocate the profit under the arm's-length principle and may invoke the GAAR in ITA 2007 s BG 1.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Directors knowingly sign and file a false IR4 that understates or omits turnover received through Stripe/PayPal, falsely reports deductible expenses, or misdescribes cross-border inventory movements to hide taxable profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994 ss 141A-141E: shortfall penalty up to 150% of the evaded tax; s 143B criminal penalty of a fine up to NZD 50,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years. Inland Revenue may also assess penal tax at 100% for abusive tax avoidance and may apply criminal asset recovery under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for directors who aided, abetted or were knowingly involved in the false return. Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and shortfall penalties, subjected to civil asset restitution orders, restrained from leaving New Zealand through an Inland Revenue departure prohibition order, disqualified from managing companies under the Companies Act 1993, and sentenced to a maximum of 5 years imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing / Shell Company Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NZ company pays disproportionately high royalties or management fees to an offshore related entity in a low-tax jurisdiction that has no real staff, premises, risk or decision-making power, while the jewellery e-commerce business sells through the NZ platform and bears all economic risk on inventory, payment gateways and customer chargebacks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act 2007 subpart GC (ss GC 1-GC 14) authorises the Commissioner to reconstruct arm's-length transfer prices; s BG 1 is the general anti-avoidance rule. TAA 1994 s 141D imposes a 100% shortfall penalty for an abusive tax position, and s 141E may impose 150% where evasion exists. Thin capitalisation rules under subpart FE further apply to shareholder debt.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for invalidity of the tax avoidance arrangement if they signed the transfer pricing documentation or structured the shell companies without commercial substance. The court can order restitution of the diverted profits plus penalty interest, issue director disqualification or blacklisting under the Companies Act 1993 ss 382-383, prohibit departure from New Zealand where tax debt is material, and impose criminal imprisonment of up to 5 years for fraudulent or reckless trading contrary to ss 135-136 and s 380 of the Companies Act 1993.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The jewellery/watch e-commerce company accepts cash, prepaid cards or virtual-asset payments from non-resident purchasers in amounts exceeding the high-value dealer threshold without conducting customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership verification, suspicious transaction reports, or an AML/CFT compliance programme, and uses the NZ Ltd as a conduit for third-party payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 ss 80-81: a body corporate faces civil penalties up to NZD 2,000,000 for serious non-compliance; infringement and criminal penalties also apply for failure to report suspicious transactions. Where money laundering is established, the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 permits assets to be restrained and forfeited as tainted property.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who were knowingly concerned in the AML/CFT breach can be made personally liable for civil penalty amounts, disqualified from being directors or managing a company, blacklisted by the regulator, and subjected to restraining orders and foreign travel bans in cross-border money laundering investigations. In aggravated cases the directors face imprisonment under the Crimes Act 1961 for money laundering and under the Companies Act 1993 s 380 for fraudulent purposes.
